variant: Character LoRA for Kyle trained on real photographs, following the Ivy route. The output is a reusable identity asset: kyle_rescue, bot_builders_champion and nightelf_hunter all carried his face by reference tokens and a master portrait, which this replaces with a trigger token.
title: Kyle — character LoRA
status: scaffolded — 6 source photographs found in the repo, short of the 20+ needed; waiting on more
source: real photographs of Kyle already in the repo (nightelf_hunter and bot_builders_champion raw folders), copied into raw/ which is git-ignored
notes: Kyle is Kevin's son; consent settled. A child's face changes fast, so every photograph should come from a narrow time window — mixing a seven-year-old and a ten-year-old trains a LoRA on the average of two faces. Generated images are excluded on purpose: kyle_rescue/seed/src_kyle_front.png is a render, and training on model output bakes in model artifacts.

dataset.subject: boy
dataset.caption_rule: Isolation Rule — caption only what varies (framing, angle, expression, clothing, background, light). Face, hair and permanent features omitted so they bind to the trigger.
inventory: kyle_ship.jpg — medium, outdoor, overcast, patterned shirt
05_build_table.jpg — group, Kyle standing centre in a white tee; confirmed by the existing bot_builders crop
08_kyle_lindsey_parkas.jpg — full body, indoor, red parka (the only full body)
04_lunch.jpg — group, which boy is Kyle needs confirming
dataset.gaps: no profile, no back of head, one full body, all frontal — the same three gaps the Ivy LoRA hit, now known in advance

training.measured_on_ivy: 0.22 it/s, ~2 h 35 m for 2000 steps, 402 MB per checkpoint
training.weights_from_ivy: 1.0 frontal close-up, 0.85 three-quarter and full body, 0.5-0.7 turning, <=0.5 profile or back
